name: Sylvia Earle
description: Sylvia Earle is among the world's foremost ocean scientists and advocates, having led more than 100 expeditions and spent over 7,000 hours underwater studying marine ecosystems and deep-sea biodiversity. She was the first female Chief Scientist of NOAA and set a solo depth record walking the ocean floor at 381 meters in a JIM suit in 1979. Her laboratory work on algae physiology and deep-ocean ecology has produced foundational reference literature on marine plant communities. Earle founded Mission Blue, a global initiative establishing a network of marine protected areas called Hope Spots, now covering tens of millions of square kilometers. She has been named Time magazine's first Hero for the Planet and holds more than a hundred honorary degrees from institutions worldwide.
